faq.q: What is included in a Marbella family boat day in 2048?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment and Spanish IVA (21%). For family days, we can add snorkel gear, paddleboards and a jet ski (on selected boats) at no extra cost. Just let us know your kids' ages and we'll prepare life jackets and any special requests.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a family with children?
faq.a: For smaller families (up to 8), the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) or Azimut 39 (12.5m) are ideal – stable, spacious and easy to board. For larger groups or multi-generational trips, the Mangusta 80 (24m) offers 12 pax and includes a free jet ski. All boats have shaded areas and safety rails. We recommend the Azimut 58 Flybridge for families who want extra deck space.

faq.q: Can we use a jet ski during our family boat day?
faq.a: Yes. On the Mangusta 80 (white or grey), a jet ski is included free with a minimum 4-hour charter (€4,719). This is the only boat in our fleet with a jet ski included. For other boats, we can arrange a jet ski rental separately – message us on WhatsApp for pricing and safety briefing details. Kids under 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

faq.q: Do we need to bring our own snorkel and paddleboard equipment?
faq.a: No. We provide snorkel masks, fins and paddleboards on request at no extra charge. Just mention your preferred activities when booking. We'll have everything ready on board. For snorkelling, we recommend the calm coves near Cabopino or Cala del Faro, where water clarity is best in the morning.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a family boat day in Marbella?
faq.a: May to September offers the warmest sea temperatures (20–26°C) and calmest conditions, ideal for snorkelling and paddleboarding. July and August are busiest – book at least 2 weeks ahead. For a quieter experience, June or September are perfect. Even in April or October, you can enjoy a sunny day with lighter winds, but bring a windbreaker.

faq.q: How long should we charter for a family day?
faq.a: We recommend 4 hours for a relaxed family day – enough time to cruise to a cove, snorkel, paddleboard, and enjoy lunch on board. If you want to include a jet ski session (on the Mangusta 80) or visit both Cabopino and Marbella Marina, go for 6–8 hours. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are available from €749 for 2 hours, but 4+ hours gives better value.

faq.q: Is the charter safe for young children?
faq.a: Absolutely. All our boats are equipped with life jackets for children, safety rails and a licensed skipper who is trained in first aid. We follow Spanish maritime safety regulations. For children under 5, we recommend the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 – both have stable hulls and low freeboard. Let us know ages when booking and we'll prepare accordingly.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on our booked day?
faq.a: Your safety is our priority. If the skipper deems conditions unsafe (high winds, thunderstorms), we'll reschedule your charter to a suitable alternative date or issue a full refund. We monitor forecasts closely and will contact you 24–48 hours before departure if any changes are needed. Most family days run in light winds below 15 knots.

data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella family boat day in 2048 that combines jetski, snorkel and paddleboard? You've come to the right place. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella's glamorous marina, and every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks and full insurance. Whether you're towing a toddler or a teenager, we'll tailor the day to your family's pace – from a gentle cruise to a jet ski adrenaline rush. Here's everything you need to know to book your perfect family adventure.

Why a family boat day in Marbella works so well

Marbella's coastline offers calm, warm waters and dozens of hidden coves, making it one of the best family boating destinations in Spain. With an average of 320 sunny days a year, you're almost guaranteed good weather. The water temperature in summer reaches 26°C – perfect for snorkelling and paddleboarding. Plus, the proximity of Puerto Banús to spots like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés means you can reach a swim spot within 20 minutes, keeping the kids entertained without long sea time.

Our family-friendly fleet: which boat to choose

We offer a range of boats to suit every family size and budget. For small families, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are the smart choice – both are Tier A boats priced from €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks and VAT. For larger families or multi-generational trips, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper – from €4,719 for 4 hours, and it includes a free jet ski. If you want extra deck space, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) offers a flybridge that kids love. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.

Combining jetski, snorkel and paddleboard: how it works

On the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free with a minimum 4-hour charter. The skipper will take you to a safe area away from swimmers, and after a safety briefing, you can enjoy a thrilling ride. For snorkelling, we provide masks and fins – ideal spots include the clear waters off Cabopino or the rocky coves near Río Verde. Paddleboards are also available on request; the calm morning waters are perfect for beginners. Your skipper will coordinate the schedule so everyone gets a turn – no queuing, no stress.

Sample itinerary for a 4-hour family day

  • 10:00 – Meet at Puerto Banús, board your boat, safety briefing.
  • 10:15 – Cruise east towards Cabopino, keeping an eye out for dolphins.
  • 10:45 – Anchor at a calm cove; first snorkel session (30–40 min).
  • 11:30 – Paddleboard exploration along the shoreline.
  • 12:15 – Jet ski session (on Mangusta 80) – 20 min per adult/teen.
  • 13:00 – Lunch on board: snacks, drinks and soft drinks.
  • 13:30 – Cruise back to Puerto Banús, spotting the Golden Mile villas.
  • 14:00 – Return to port, with time for a stroll around the marina.

Pro tips for a smooth family day

  • Book early – July and August slots fill up 3–4 weeks ahead.
  • Choose the morning – Sea conditions are calmest before 11:00.
  • Bring a windbreaker – Even in summer, sea breezes can be cool.
  • Pack reef-safe sunscreen – We care about the marine environment.
  • Tell us about dietary needs – We can adjust snacks and drinks.
